signals.headline: ‘Absolutely unacceptable’: Japan condemns visit by Vladimir Putin to disputed Kuril Islands
signals.summary: The Japanese government has reacted angrily to Vladimir Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, which are claimed by both Tokyo and Moscow.
keyTakeaways: Japan’s foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, summoned the Russian ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev, while the prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, called Putin’s actions “absolutely unacceptable”.
The Soviet Union declared war on Japan in August 1945 as Tokyo was about to surrender, and the dispute has prevented the two nations from signing a formal peace treaty.
About 17,000 Japanese formerly lived on the islands, which today are occupied by about 20,000 Russian citizens.
signals.whyItMatters: The Russian president acknowledged Abe’s actions in his remarks on Wednesday and went to call the recent sanctions “unprovoked”.

ja.headline: プーチン氏の北方四島訪問 日本「断固容認できない」
ja.summary: ロシアのプーチン大統領が北方四島を初めて訪問したことに対し、日本政府が強い反発を示している。北方四島は日本とロシアの双方が領有権を主張してきた地域だ。
keyTakeaways: 茂木敏充外相はロシアのノズドレフ大使を呼び、高市早苗首相はプーチン氏の行動を「断固容認できない」と述べた。
ソ連は1945年8月、日本が降伏を目前にした時期に対日参戦し、この領土問題が両国の平和条約締結を妨げてきた。
かつて島には約一万七千人の日本人が暮らしていたが、現在は約二万人のロシア国民が住む。
ja.whyItMatters: プーチン氏は水曜の発言で安倍元首相の対応に触れつつ、最近の制裁を「不当な仕打ち」と呼んだ。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So Putin visited some islands and Japan is furious about it?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes. He made his first visit to the Kuril Islands, which both Japan and Russia claim.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Why does that touch such a nerve?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: The dispute goes back to 1945, when the Soviet Union declared war on Japan just as Tokyo was about to surrender.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And that's still unresolved after all this time?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It is. It's actually the reason Japan and Russia have never signed a formal peace treaty.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What did Japan actually do in response?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: The foreign minister summoned Russia's ambassador, and the prime minister called Putin's visit 'absolutely unacceptable'.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Who actually lives there now?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: About 20,000 Russian citizens live there today, though roughly 17,000 Japanese once called the islands home.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And Putin's side of it?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: He referenced Japan's own past actions and also called recent sanctions against Russia 'unprovoked'.

signals.headline: RSC postpones Othello while leading actor Sharon D Clarke has cancer treatment
signals.summary: The Royal Shakespeare Company has announced that it will postpone its radical production of Othello starring Sharon D Clarke, while the Olivier-winning actor undergoes treatment for cancer.
keyTakeaways: Clarke, 60, is best known for her role as Lola Griffin in the BBC medical drama Holby City, as well as for her theatrical performances in Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom and Caroline, or Change.
In a statement on Thursday, Clarke said: “I would like to thank all the beautiful people at the RSC for their understanding, love, support and healing energy.
Othello will be my north star as I undergo treatment.”
signals.whyItMatters: The production, directed by Monique Touko, was scheduled to run from 13 February to 3 April 2027 at the Swan theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon.

ja.headline: RSC、『オセロー』上演を延期 主演女優の療養のため
ja.summary: 英国のロイヤル・シェイクスピア・カンパニー（RSC）は、シャロン・D・クラーク氏主演の新演出『オセロー』の上演延期を発表した。オリヴィエ賞受賞歴を持つクラーク氏は、がんの治療に専念するという。
keyTakeaways: クラーク氏（60）はBBCの医療ドラマ『ホルビー・シティ』のローラ・グリフィン役、また舞台『マ・レイニーのブラックボトム』や『キャロライン、あるいは変化』での演技で知られる。
木曜の声明でクラーク氏は「RSCの心優しい皆さんの理解と愛、支え、そして癒しの力に感謝したい」と述べた。
「治療を受けるあいだ、『オセロー』は私にとって北極星のような存在になる」と語った。
ja.whyItMatters: モニーク・トゥーコ氏が演出を手がける本作は、2027年2月13日から4月3日までストラトフォード・アポン・エイヴォンのスワン劇場で上演予定だった。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: I saw the RSC's postponing Othello — what happened?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Sharon D Clarke, who's starring in it, is undergoing treatment for cancer, so the production's been paused.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: She's the actor from Holby City, right?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That's her — Lola Griffin. She's also known for Ma Rainey's Black Bottom and Caroline, or Change.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Has she said anything about it herself?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, she thanked everyone at the RSC for their support, and said Othello will be her 'north star' during treatment.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That's a lovely way to put it. When was the show meant to open?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It was set to run from 13 February to 3 April 2027 at the Swan theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is there a new date yet?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Not yet — for now it's simply postponed while she focuses on her health.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Well, I hope she recovers well.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Same here — and it sounds like the whole production is standing by her.

signals.headline: Photos: See the best photos from the solar eclipse
signals.summary: The Picture Show Millions of people in Europe stepped outside this evening to watch a spectacular sunset with a solar eclipse.
keyTakeaways: People record a video of the moon partially covering the sun during a solar eclipse, as seen from Berlin, Germany.
A fish jumps out of the water during a solar eclipse as the moon partially covers the sun and briefly dims the afternoon light along the coast of Fregene, near Rome.
A beachgoer wearing special eclipse glasses looks up during the beginning phase of a solar eclipse at Puerto de Sagunto beach near Valencia, Spain.
signals.whyItMatters: The moon completely covers the sun during a total solar eclipse as seen from the Javalambre Astrophysical Observatory in Arcos de las Salinas, near Teruel, Spain, August 12, 2026.

ja.headline: 欧州の空を彩った日食、その瞬間をカメラが捉えた
ja.summary: この夕方、欧州各地で人々が外に出て、日食と重なる壮麗な夕焼けを見上げた。ベルリンからスペインまで、各地の海辺や街角で人々が空を見つめた光景が広がった。
keyTakeaways: ドイツ・ベルリンでは、月が太陽の一部を隠す様子を人々がスマートフォンで撮影した
ローマ近郊フレジェネの海岸では、日食で午後の光がわずかに薄れる中、魚が水面から跳ねる場面が見られた
スペイン・バレンシア近郊のプエルト・デ・サグント海岸では、専用の遮光グラスをかけた人が日食の始まりを見上げていた
ja.whyItMatters: スペイン・テルエル近郊、アルコス・デ・ラス・サリナスのハバランブレ天文台からは、月が太陽を完全に覆う皆既日食の様子が観測された。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So people across Europe just stopped to watch the sky tonight?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, a solar eclipse lined up right at sunset, which made it even more striking.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Where were people watching from?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Places like Berlin, Valencia, and along the coast near Rome all caught different views of it.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What did it actually look like?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: In Berlin, people filmed the moon slowly covering part of the sun. Near Rome, the light dimmed enough that a fish leaping from the water became part of the scene.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And in Spain?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: At a beach near Valencia, someone wearing eclipse glasses looked up just as the moon began sliding across the sun.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Was it a full eclipse anywhere?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, at an observatory near Teruel, Spain, the moon fully covered the sun, giving a clear view of a total eclipse.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Sounds like a quiet kind of wonder people shared together.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly. A shared moment, looking up at the same sky.

signals.headline: Flock boss admits surveillance firm took too long to act over police abuse
signals.summary: Flock, the US surveillance firm, is rolling out new safeguards to prevent police misuse of its technology which, its founder and chief executive admits, should have happened sooner.
keyTakeaways: Police have used Flock to track romantic partners, external and stalk strangers, leading to growing public backlash against the company.
Flock is cutting the number of days most data is retained, from 30 days to seven and abnormal searches and uses will also automatically be flagged.
Flock cameras have been used by police to not only track former and current romantic partners, but in one case, even a woman who had had an abortion, external.
signals.whyItMatters: This was around the time that Amazon's Ring, a doorbell camera firm, cancelled a partnership with Flock after an outcry over a Super Bowl advert which sparked concern about unwanted surveillance.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So this is the company behind those license plate cameras police use?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, Flock. And its own boss admits they took too long to stop police misusing it.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Misusing it how?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Police have used it to track romantic partners, and in one case, a woman who'd had an abortion.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That's unsettling. What's changing now?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Data will now be kept for seven days instead of thirty, and unusual searches will be flagged automatically.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Did something push them to act now?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Partly. Amazon's Ring pulled out of a partnership with Flock after backlash over an advert during the Super Bowl.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So public pressure made the difference.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It seems so. The company is admitting the safeguards should have come much sooner.

signals.headline: Are teens on ebikes the ‘new Hells Angels’? Not so fast, boomers
signals.summary: They are often marketed as ebikes, despite exceeding speed and power rules set for actual ebikes.
keyTakeaways: Are teens on ebikes the ‘new Hells Angels’?
The Los Angeles Times recently dubbed them the “ new Hells Angels ”.
In this regulatory wild west, legal ebikes are caught in the crossfire.
signals.whyItMatters: Biking advocates point to existing rules for actual ebikes and argue the majority of riders are not thrill-seeking speedsters but commuters who’ve tapped into ebikes’ convenience and low environmental impact as a replacement for local car trips.

ja.headline: 電動バイクの若者たち、本当に『危険な存在』か
ja.summary: 電動バイクに乗る若者たちが「新たなヘルズエンジェルス」と呼ばれている。だが多くは正規のebikeとして売られながら、実際には速度や出力の基準を超えている。
keyTakeaways: 電動バイクの若者は『新たなヘルズエンジェルス』なのか
ロサンゼルス・タイムズ紙が最近そう呼んだ
規制の空白の中、正規のebikeも巻き添えになっている
ja.whyItMatters: 自転車推進派は、多くの利用者がスリルを求める暴走者ではなく、車移動に代わる手軽で環境負荷の低い通勤手段として電動バイクを選んでいると指摘する。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So are teens on ebikes really being called the 'new Hells Angels'?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That's the phrase the Los Angeles Times used, yes.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That sounds pretty alarming. Is it fair?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Not quite. Many of these bikes are marketed as ebikes but actually exceed the speed and power limits set for real ebikes.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So it's more of a labeling problem than a teens problem?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: In many cases, yes. There's a regulatory gap right now, and legal ebikes are getting caught in the crossfire.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What do people who bike a lot say about this?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Advocates point out that most riders on proper ebikes aren't speedsters at all.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What are they using them for, then?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Mostly commuting. They're replacing short local car trips, which also helps cut down on environmental impact.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So the real story is about rules catching up, not teens causing chaos.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That's the heart of it, yes.
